text: **dsh-session-notification**（DSH Web 插件）：在会话运行结束、失败、等待回答或请求授权时提醒你。它在 Web 客户端观察会话状态和待处理交互，并通过设置面板提供通知与提示音控制。主要功能包括区分完成与失败、按主会话或全部会话筛选并可等待子会话结束、播放四种内置或自定义音频，以及在获准后显示浏览器系统通知。适合需要离开当前标签页或同时运行多个会话、希望及时知道任务进展的 DSH 用户。浏览器通知默认关闭，启用时需授予浏览器通知权限；偏好和自定义音频保存在本地浏览器。

dsh-session-notification (DSH Web plugin) alerts on run completion, failure, questions, and permission requests. It offers session scope and subagent waiting controls, built-in or custom sounds, and browser notifications. Preferences and custom audio are stored locally.
想让 DSH 会话结束时提醒我，不用一直盯着页面。
任务运行失败或者正常完成时，能不能用不同提示音通知我？
Agent 等我回答问题或批准操作时，希望收到提醒。
我同时跑多个子会话，想只在主会话和子任务都结束后再提醒。
能不能给不同类型的会话事件设置不同声音，或者上传自己的音频？
切到其他应用或把标签页放到后台时，我想收到系统通知。
Can I get an alert when a DSH run finishes or fails while I am away from the tab?
I want separate sounds for questions, permission requests, and completed sessions.
How can I wait for all spawned sessions to finish before the main session notification?
**dsh-session-notification** 的功能「会话状态提醒」：观察会话运行状态变化，将正常结束与运行错误分类，并在问题或授权交互出现时产生对应提醒。首次观察到已空闲的会话不会触发历史通知。
**dsh-session-notification** 的功能「通知范围与子会话等待」：可通知全部会话、仅主会话，或等主会话的运行中子会话结束后再提醒；当前正在查看的会话也可按隐藏、失焦或始终提醒设置。
**dsh-session-notification** 的功能「提示音与自定义音频」：为完成、失败、提问和授权事件选择内置音效、静音或上传自定义音频，并调整总音量；设置页可试听。
**dsh-session-notification** 的功能「浏览器系统通知」：在设置中请求浏览器权限并启用系统通知；通知带会话信息，点击后可聚焦页面并打开对应会话。
dsh-session-notification 使用前须知：浏览器系统通知默认关闭，开启前需通过用户操作申请浏览器权限；偏好设置与自定义音频保存在浏览器本地。

text:
@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · The four notification kinds：| Kind | When it fires | Default sound |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Session completed | A turn ends normally (`turn/end` completed) | chime |
| Session failed | A turn breaks with an error, or the host reports an agent error | fault |
| Question asked | The agent is waiting for your answer (`question/requested`) | pop |
| Permission requested | The agent requests an authorized operation (`approval/requested`) | alert |

@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · The four notification kinds：Each kind can be enabled or disabled and reassigned to any of the four built-in sound effects (or muted). The four sounds are synthesized with Web Audio — no audio files are shipped — and the master volume is adjustable with the official-style slider (0–100%). A fixed loudness boost (~+6 dB) with a soft limiter on the playback chain makes every sound noticeably louder without distortion; custom audio feeds the same chain. The shared AudioContext is suspended as soon as playback is over and resumed by the next sound, so an idle notification never keeps the system audio stream (or a macOS sleep assertion) open.

@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · Custom audio：Beyond the four built-in sounds, each kind accepts **your own audio file** (mp3/ogg/wav, up to 1 MB): pick Custom audio on a kind's row to upload one, and it replaces the built-in for that kind — with a Replace and remove affordance, plus the Custom audio in use tag. Custom files are stored browser-locally (they are device media, not shared preferences).

@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · Browser notifications & the quiet default：Browser (system-level) notifications are **off by default**; turning the switch on asks for the browser's permission first (a user gesture). Once granted, a notification is shown when the event's session is not the one you are reading, or when the tab is in the background. Notifications carry the **page's own icon** (the favicon the harness serves). A completed session's notification carries its **final reply text** (the last assistant message). **Clicking a notification** focuses the page and opens that session (Web and desktop alike). The Test notification button in the section sends one immediately to verify the channel once permission is granted.

@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · Browser notifications & the quiet default：The session you are reading stays **quiet by default** — its own events don't interrupt you while you are actually watching it. The **Current session alerts** picker widens that:

@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · Browser notifications & the quiet default：| The session you are reading, while you are… | Hidden or minimized (default) | When switched away | Always |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| watching it with DSH focused | 🔕 Quiet | 🔕 Quiet | ✅ Alert |
| switched to another app, DSH still on screen | 🔕 Quiet | ✅ **Alert** | ✅ Alert |
| in another tab, or the window is minimized | ✅ Alert | ✅ Alert | ✅ Alert |

@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · Browser notifications & the quiet default：**Notify for** picks the scope (default **Main, after subagents**): *All sessions* alerts for every session including subagents; *Main only* alerts for the main session as soon as it goes idle; *Main, after subagents* holds that alert until every subagent the main session spawned has finished, so a run that only paused between subagent waves never interrupts you early (failures always alert immediately).

@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · Desktop app：The plugin runs unchanged inside the dsh desktop application — the Electron shell loads the same Web client and plugin graph. Desktop notifications are **native OS notifications**: the shell grants notification permission by default, so turning **Browser notifications** on is enough and no permission prompt appears. A notification carries the **application icon** (the page favicon is used on Web; under `dsh-app://` the page icon is skipped so the packaged app icon shows instead), is marked **silent** so the OS alert sound never doubles the plugin's own sound, and clicking one restores/focuses the window through the shell's app activation and opens that session's conversation — closing the window only hides it.

@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · Desktop app：The desktop app owns `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop` and the CLI refuses to manage it, so install the plugin from the app's **Plugins** page (Settings → Plugins) instead of `dsh plugin --profile desktop`. Preferences are browser-local to that renderer, so they are separate from the Web profile's.
@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · The Notifications settings section：The plugin registers a **Notifications** section in the settings panel (Settings ⚙ → Notifications):

@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · The Notifications settings section：- **Browser notifications** master switch (+ permission state and an enable button),
- **Current session alerts** picker (Hidden or minimized only / When switched away / Always),
- **Notify for** picker (All sessions / Main only / Main, after subagents),
- **Sound** master switch,
- **Volume** slider (0–100%),
- one row per notification kind: enable switch, custom-audio upload, sound picker (the official dropdown menu), and a Preview button,
- a Test notification button on the browser-notifications row (verifies the OS channel once permission is granted).

@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · The Notifications settings section：Preferences are stored **browser-locally** (localStorage) under the `dsh-session-notification` key — no host settings-namespace exposure required — so they persist across sessions and sync across tabs, and never depend on a harness change.
@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · How it works：The browser half watches the sessions list snapshot and each session's conversation snapshot — no polling, no new wire channels:

@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · How it works：- A session's `running` edge true→false ends a run; the run is classified **failed** when a new `turn-error` node or a host `agent-error` appeared during it, otherwise **completed** (a failure that a retry recovered reads as completed).
- A completion raises nothing while the host still has work that will start another turn by itself (a queued follow-up, or a goal round the driver still owes): that idle edge is a pause, and the continuation's own end notifies. A completed or failed notice is titled by the run's latest user message, falling back to the session title.
- A pending-interaction edge (`question` / `approval`) raises the question / permission kinds, with the question text or the tool name+reason in the notification body.
- Sessions already idle (or already pending) when the plugin loads raise nothing.

@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · Development：- `yarn run build` — builds the browser bundle (`lib/client.js`) and the Node half (`lib/index.js`).
- `src/client/notification-service.ts` — the engine (classification) and dispatcher (gating); `src/client/settings-store.ts` — the settings section bridge; `src/client/NotificationsSection.tsx` — the section UI; `src/client/sounds.ts` + `src/client/custom-audio.ts` — the built-in and custom sounds.
- `yarn test` — behavior tests; `yarn run typecheck` — type gate.
- dsh 0.2.1-rc.2: the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` types install from npm as devDependencies (`^0.2.1-rc.2`, with the now-stable `@deepseek-ai/cordis` ^4.0.5 and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` ^3.18.5 matching the dsh peers); no checkout path mappings. The 0.2.1 line removed the runtime invariant-plugin mechanism (as of alpha.1), so the former `./invariant` companion is gone.
- Node-half changes need a `dsh web` restart; browser-bundle changes need a rebuild (`yarn run build`) — a `--dev` server hot-reloads them.

@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · Known limitations：- Failure detection reads the conversation snapshot, which the client only maintains for sessions that have been opened; a session that runs without ever being opened notifies as completed even on failure.
- Browser notifications require permission, and sound playback requires the page to have user activation (the browser's autoplay policy) — both are normal for browser apps and resolve as soon as the user interacts with the GUI.
- Custom audio files live in the browser (localStorage), so they do not follow you across browsers or profiles.
- The browser half is event-driven from the sessions list; it does not observe the raw event stream, so a run that starts and finishes between two list snapshots could in principle be missed (the host sends a status flip per edge, so this does not happen in practice).
- Goal *activation* is process-local and never on the wire: a goal left `active` but disarmed (for example after a restart) reads as a continuation, so its idle edge stays unannounced until the goal changes or is resumed.
- Background-job rosters are loaded only for the session you are viewing, so a job that finishes
@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · Model Experience：None. The plugin is a pure client-side observer over the already-logged session state; nothing here reaches a model request.
@dingyi222666/dsh-session-notification README · KV Cache effect：None; this package neither assembles nor sends provider requests.
